newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu CEO sees improving profitability.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu CEO sees improving profitability.

text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy's chief executive Jyrki Juusela said in the company's 1996 annual report received on Monday that he expected a definite improvement in profitability this year.
"The past year turned out to be markedly weaker for Outokumpu than we expected at the beginning of the year," Juusela wrote, adding, however, that: "... our competitiveness is clearly improving."
"Definite improvement in profitability can ... be expected during the current year stemming from full capacity utilisation and improved cost efficiency," Juusela said.
"There is also the possibility of a long-awaited zinc price increase," he said.
In 1996, Outokumpu's profit before extraordinary items fell to 229 million markka from 1.48 billion the previous year.

Earnings weakened in all of its three main business groups -- Base Metals posted a 700 million markka loss before extras, Copper Products' profit fell to 74 million from 164 million and Stainless Steel's profit fell to 616 million from 1.78 billion.
Looking ahead, Juusela said: "We are convinced that we have good opportunities, also for the longer term, to achieve profitable growth in all our main business areas."
"Our activities to enhance group operations and an extensive investment programme in our core businesses will contribute to improvement in profitability and efficiency during 1997 and 1998," he said.
"I trust that we have every opportunity in the coming year to improve our financial result and again raise our dividends," Juusela said.
The board proposed a 1.00 markka dividend for 1996, down from 1.80 markka on the group's 1995 earnings.
